segments.text: The false positive paradox.
segments.caption: The false positive paradox.

segments.text: A test that's 99 percent accurate, a result that's usually wrong, ten thousand people to prove it, and why doctors always retest. Save this one!
segments.caption: A test that's 99% accurate, a result that's usually wrong, 10,000 people to prove it, and why doctors always retest. Save this one!

segments.text: A rare disease affects one in every thousand people.
segments.caption: A rare disease affects 1 in every 1,000 people.

segments.text: You take a test that's 99 percent accurate. It comes back positive.
segments.caption: You take a test that's 99% accurate. It comes back positive.

segments.text: What's the chance you actually have the disease? Comment your guess before the answer.
segments.caption: What's the chance you actually have the disease? Comment your guess before the answer.

segments.text: Most people say 99 percent. Some say 90.
segments.caption: Most people say 99%. Some say 90.

segments.text: The real answer: about nine percent. More than nine out of ten positive results are false alarms.
segments.caption: The real answer: about 9%. More than 9 out of 10 positive results are false alarms.

segments.text: Here's how. Picture ten thousand people.
segments.caption: Here's how. Picture 10,000 people.

segments.text: One in a thousand is sick, so ten people really have the disease.
segments.caption: 1 in 1,000 is sick, so 10 people really have the disease.

segments.text: The test is 99 percent accurate, so it catches all ten of them. Ten true positives.
segments.caption: The test is 99% accurate, so it catches all 10 of them. 10 true positives.

segments.text: But here's the twist. The other nine thousand nine hundred and ninety people are healthy.
segments.caption: But here's the twist. The other 9,990 people are healthy.

segments.text: And the test is wrong for one percent of them. One percent of almost ten thousand is about a hundred people.
segments.caption: And the test is wrong for 1% of them. 1% of almost 10,000 is about 100 people.

segments.text: A hundred healthy people told they're sick. Those are false positives.
segments.caption: 100 healthy people told they're sick. Those are false positives.

segments.text: Now count all the positives: ten true, plus about a hundred false. About a hundred and ten.
segments.caption: Now count all the positives: 10 true, plus about 100 false. About 110.

segments.text: Only ten of those hundred and ten are really sick. Ten divided by a hundred and ten is about nine percent.
segments.caption: Only 10 of those 110 are really sick. 10 divided by 110 is about 9%.

segments.text: The trap is the base rate. The disease is so rare that the healthy crowd is huge.
segments.caption: The trap is the base rate. The disease is so rare that the healthy crowd is huge.

segments.text: A tiny error rate on a huge crowd creates more false alarms than there are real cases.
segments.caption: A tiny error rate on a huge crowd creates more false alarms than there are real cases.

segments.text: Ignoring how rare something is: that's called base rate neglect.
segments.caption: Ignoring how rare something is: that's called base rate neglect.

segments.text: That's why doctors retest. Among the hundred and ten positives, a second test clears almost all the false alarms.
segments.caption: That's why doctors retest. Among the 110 positives, a second test clears almost all the false alarms.

segments.text: After two positive tests, the chance you're really sick jumps to about ninety percent.
segments.caption: After two positive tests, the chance you're really sick jumps to about 90%.

segments.text: It's everywhere.
segments.caption: It's everywhere.

segments.text: Your bank blocks your card for fraud, but it was just you shopping. Airport scanners beep at innocent bags. Spam filters bin real emails.
segments.caption: Your bank blocks your card for fraud, but it was just you shopping. Airport scanners beep at innocent bags. Spam filters bin real emails.

segments.text: When the thing you're looking for is rare, most alarms are false.
segments.caption: When the thing you're looking for is rare, most alarms are false.

segments.text: So remember: a positive result depends on how rare the thing is, not just how accurate the test is.
segments.caption: So remember: a positive result depends on how rare the thing is, not just how accurate the test is.
